hushgram.body:
## [0.0.12](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/compare/v0.0.11...v0.0.12) (2026-10-16)

### Features

* **Instagram - Download any story:** A video story you filmed gets Download as photo under Download now, which saves one still picture from it at full size. Download still saves the video. Asked for in #215.
* **Instagram - Download any reel:** New switch under Download, Download audio, off by default. It adds Download audio to a reel's menu, which saves just the sound as an M4A file to Recordings (Music on Android 11 and older). Asked for in #216.
* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** New switch under Tab bar, Hide Messages on Home's header, off by default. It's for accounts that still have Instagram's Messages button at the top of Home and turned on Show the Messages tab, which leaves Messages in two places. Asked for in #210.
* **Instagram - Show if a profile follows you:** New switch under Profiles, Recent unfollowers, off by default. Scroll to the end of your own Followers list and anyone missing since last time shows under Who unfollowed you, with the date. Asked for in #208.
* **Instagram - Show if a profile follows you:** Recent unfollowers only reads the list Instagram already loaded, so nothing extra is asked of Instagram. The list stays on your phone, kept apart for each account, and Clear unfollower list wipes it. Asked for in #208.
* **Instagram - Story ring size:** Ring color has Teal now, a blue-green that stays easy to see on white and black pages alike. Asked for in #206.
* **Instagram - Hide reels by caption words:** New patch with a switch and a Blocked words list under Reels, off and empty by default. A reel in the Reels tab goes when its caption holds one of your words or phrases, hashtags included. Asked for in #192.
* **Instagram - Hide reels by caption words:** Case doesn't matter. Put a comma or a new line between words, so a list from Hushfeed pastes straight in. Reels you open from a profile, search or a chat still play. Asked for in #192.
* **Instagram - Hide reels by caption words:** Also on Home under the list hides posts on Home with those words in their caption too. That part needs Hide suggested posts in your build. Asked for in #192.
* **Instagram - HushGram settings:** HushGram's settings come in Italian when your phone is set to Italian. Like the other translations, it's a first draft that a native reader can still improve. Asked for in #194.
* **Instagram - Download any video:** New switch under Downloads, Save every page without asking, off by default. With Download button on feed posts on, a tap on a carousel saves all of its pages at once instead of asking which. Asked for in #190.
* **Instagram - Show a reel's exact time:** New switch, Show how long ago a reel was posted, off by default. It adds a line under the reel's time like 1d 2h 5m ago, in HushGram's language. Searching the patch's name finds both its choices now. Asked for in #195.
* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** Tab order under Tab bar opens a new list, Show and reorder tabs. Check a tab to put it on the bar and drag its handle to move it. Reset brings back Instagram's tabs. Nothing changes until you tap OK. Asked for in #207.

### Bug Fixes

* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** Always Home opens Home again with your tabs reordered in Tab order, and after you swipe Instagram away from recent apps. Both used to open Reels. Coming back while Instagram is still open keeps you where you were. Reported in #55.
* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** Start tab set to Search, Reels or Profile opens on its tab with the tabs reordered too. The diagnostic report counts each start and why a start tab was skipped. Reported in #55.
* **Instagram - Keep a seek bar on Reels:** With Seek bar like DM videos or Bigger seek bar on, the played part and the handle slide along steadily. They used to jump about ten times a second, as often as Instagram updates it. Reported in #10.
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** With Show content behind the tab bar on, a reel's comment box sat under the navigation bar until the keyboard came up, and other sheets could lose their bottom row. Sheets get their usual space back now. Reported in #209.
* **Instagram - Keep a seek bar on Reels:** A new reel's seek bar starts at the beginning right away. It used to show the last reel's spot for a moment and then jump back to the start, which was most of what you'd see when swiping quickly. Reported in #10.
* **Instagram - Font:** A color emoji font picked as the Font shows in the emoji row above the comment box now, not only in the box. That row used to keep Instagram's old emoji pictures, even after a restart. Reported in #166.
* **Instagram - Font:** A text font or a black and white emoji font leaves that row alone, since it would draw it in black. Emoji the file doesn't have still look like your phone's. Reported in #166.
* **Instagram - Font:** The bio under a profile's name takes the font you picked too. Instagram draws it with its newer text system, which loaded its own font and skipped the swap, and other text drawn that way follows now as well. Reported in #166.
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** Once Hide the tab bar on Reels slides the pill away, the reel runs to the bottom of the screen instead of leaving a black band where the pill was. It makes room again when the pill comes back. Reported in #170.
* **Instagram - Hide suggested posts:** Hide videos, Hide photos, Hide carousels, Hide posts you've liked and Hidden accounts now catch suggested posts on Home too. Instagram 451 wraps each suggested post in a unit those switches didn't look inside. Found while working on #192.
* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** With Hide the Search tab on, the Search button on Home's header opens search again on phones that swipe between tabs. It used to show a note asking you to turn the switch off. Back returns to Home. Reported in #204.
* **Instagram - Download any reel:** The Download button beside a reel now uses Instagram's own icon made for that column, the one Save's is drawn from, so it's the same size and line weight as the buttons above it instead of bigger and bolder. Reported in #198.
* **Instagram - Glass tab bar:** With the floating glass bar on, a chat's message box sat too low, half under the keyboard or behind navigation buttons. Chats keep the right space again, and leaving one no longer leaves a black strip under the pill. Reported in #196.
* **Instagram - Full screen Reels and Home:** With full screen on, opening Instagram straight onto Reels, or coming back to Reels from HushGram settings or a chat, could leave black strips at the top and bottom until you switched tabs. Reels fills the screen either way now. Reported in #200.
* **Instagram - Full screen Reels and Home:** With Full screen Home on, the first tab you opened from Home, like Messages or your profile, slid up under the status bar until you switched again. That tab leaves room for the bar now. Reported in #203.
* **Instagram - Show if a profile follows you:** On a profile with no name, the Follows you or Doesn't follow you label sat on top of the post and follower counts. It takes the line where the name would be now. Reported in #157.
* **Instagram - Full screen Reels and Home:** With full screen on, the keyboard covered a reel's comment box, which sat one navigation bar too low once the keyboard brought that bar back. It sits right above the keyboard now, with the glass tab bar on too. Reported in #209.

### Improvements

* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** Pausing, playing or liking a reel with a tap, and tapping Save or Download, no longer bring Burn-in guard's faded buttons back. Other buttons, the caption, the bars and swiping to the next reel still do. Asked for in #162.
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** New Dim after choice under Burn-in guard sets how long it waits before fading, from at once to 10 seconds. It starts at 5, as before. Asked for in #162.
* **Instagram - Clean up Reels:** Burn-in guard dims a reel's seek bar now, and the time HushGram shows next to it fades along with it. The Not interested and Interested buttons under some reels fade too. Reported in #162.
* **Instagram - HushGram settings:** Searching for Download any video now also finds Download button on feed posts and the switch under it.
* **Instagram - Hide the Reels tab:** Listed under Interface in Morphe's patch list now, next to the glass tab bar, since most of its switches are about the tab bar. That keeps Reels short enough to scan with the new caption words patch in it.

### Validation

Validation: 5375 runtime tests passed locally. All 1959 patch tests passed too.

hushtelegram.title: v0.0.18
hushtelegram.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.18 has 68 patches for telegram.org's Telegram 13.0.3 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71839) and the official Telegram beta 13.0.3 (`org.telegram.messenger.beta`, also 71839). Sixty-four are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. This release moves to Telegram 13.0.3. Telegram 13 dropped the menu that slid in from the left, so the new `Side menu` switch draws one again with your name and the screens it used to reach. Search can stay inside your own chats with `Search only my chats`, and `Lock HushTelegram settings` keeps every setting read-only until a 24 hour wait runs out. There's also a `How to translate` box for AI translation, a folder to open at launch, a compact bottom bar and a way to keep your location from Mini Apps. Patching takes about half as long as it did.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** Moved to Telegram 13.0.3, telegram.org's build and the official beta (both version code 71839). Every patch carried over without a change.
* **Telegram:** The descriptions in Morphe Manager now mention the switches that were added inside existing patches, so you can see what **Hide popular apps**, **Faster downloads**, **Repair Firebase push registration** and nine others also bring before you patch. The patch names didn't change, so your saved selection carries over.
* **Telegram:** **Black and white launch logo** shows the white logo on black every time now, with AMOLED black on and your phone in dark mode. Before, Telegram's blue launch screen came back whenever Android reopened a Telegram it had closed in the background, since Android skips the launch screen an app names for itself in that case. The logo now sits in Telegram's own dark launch screen instead. With AMOLED black off you get Telegram's usual launch screen, except after Android has closed Telegram in the background in dark mode, when it's the black one. Reported in #6.
* **Telegram:** HushTelegram settings can drop the cards. **Settings look** at the top of Look and feel switches every page to plain rows with a thin line between them, the text closer to the edge and section titles in the accent color, and dialogs' choices follow. Tap it again for the cards. The status card at the top keeps its card either way. It's only how the settings screen looks, so settings files and Quick setups leave it out and Pause doesn't touch it. Asked for in #18.
* **Telegram:** **Hide phone number** no longer says it covers your number in the side menu, in Morphe Manager or in its settings line. Telegram 13 dropped its side menu, and the new **Side menu** switch shows your name but never your number.
* **Telegram:** **Hide folder tab counters** adds an **Open a folder at launch** switch, off by default, with a **Folder to open** row under it. Pick one of your folders and the chat list opens on it instead of All Chats. Each account keeps its own pick on this phone, and your folder order and the folders on Telegram's servers aren't touched. A folder that's gone, renamed or locked falls back to All Chats (a new folder that takes a deleted one's place doesn't count as your pick), and the chat pickers for sharing and forwarding open as they always have.
* **Telegram:** **Hide popular apps** adds a **Find names in styled letters** switch, off by default. With it on, searching your chats and contacts finds names written in decorative letters (𝐁𝐨𝐥𝐝, 𝘐𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘤, Ｗｉｄｅ, circled and the like) when you type ordinary ones. Names still show as they're written, numbers and other alphabets aren't touched, and a name found this way isn't highlighted.
* **Telegram:** Export diagnostic report has a third choice, **Preview the report**. It shows the report as it would be shared, with a box for each part, such as hook status or the selected events. Untick anything you'd rather keep to yourself and Copy or Save takes only what's still ticked. Cancel leaves nothing on the clipboard and no file behind. A very long report shows its first 30,000 characters and says how much there is. A file saved with a part left out isn't called the full report.

Accounts show as 1, 2 and so on, never by name or number, and a reply that can't be tied to one account isn't shown as anyone's. The diagnostic report carries the same lines.

* **Tooling:** Every build graph this repository owns uses Guava 33.7.2 now, the release that fixes CVE-2026-102554. That includes the lint and annotation tools the Android plugin loads on its own. * **Tooling:** A device build now waits its turn in the machine's build queue before it starts patching, and the patcher runs with a capped heap and two processors so it doesn't crowd out builds already running.
* **Tooling:** A release can't skip the build advisory scan anymore. * **Tooling:** A release no longer stops when the GitHub description names no version, patch count or Telegram build. That description is left as written, and one that names any of them is still kept current.
* **Tooling:** A device build now clears out what a killed one left behind. When `patch-for-device.ps1` starts, it deletes any `run-` folder in the output folder that no running build owns, the argument file with the signing password included. Each build records its process and start time in its folder, so a build that's still running is never touched. One whose process can't be read, such as a build started as administrator, is left alone too.

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.0.3 from telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android). The [official beta](https://telegram.org/dl/android/apk-public-beta) 13.0.3 works too, and both have version code 71839. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from v0.0.17? That one was built for 13.0.2, so patch the new 13.0.3 APK and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put one over the other. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram won't send you a login code, register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps). Use only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

1360 runtime tests and 487 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints. All 68 patches applied without forcing to Telegram 13.0.3 and to the 13.0.3 beta, both version code 71839. The release receipt checked each patched app's manifest, native libraries, resources and alignment.

On a Samsung phone running Android 16, a 13.0.3 build from the same patch code installed over the 13.0.2 one and stayed signed in. A swipe on the chat list's title bar opened the side menu, its HushTelegram settings and Settings rows opened their pages, and Back closed it. The patched 13.0.3 beta started and opened HushTelegram settings on an Android emulator.

The media tabs and the Chats tab with a chat or date filter don't search for typed text either, so they keep what they showed. A contact you find by typing a "+" phone number turns up in the Chats tab again with the switch on. The Posts tab and search inside a chat still go to Telegram, and the switch's description now says which parts of the main search stay on the phone. With the switch off or HushTelegram paused, search works the way Telegram's does.
* **Telegram:** The settings home page has a new row under Quick setups, **Lock HushTelegram settings**. Once it's on, every setting on the screen is read-only. Switches, Quick setups (Back to defaults too), Pause, the choosers and settings import all stay as they are and a short note says why. To change something again, tap **Start unlock** and wait 24 hours. The row shows the time left and can cancel the wait, and turning the phone's clock back past the start begins it again. Resume, Debug logging and Export settings still work while it's locked. Asked for in #17.
* **Telegram:** The AI translation service has a **How to translate** box. Write how you want things translated in your own words (keep it casual, leave names alone, a word list) and it goes to your AI service along with each message, up to 1,000 characters. It's optional and stays on this phone with your key. Google's web translate doesn't use it, and it's still there if you switch back to an AI service later. Asked for in #6.
* **Telegram:** **Hide messages by keyword** turns away an expression whose count only makes work, like `/(?:(?=x)){16777215}(?!x)/`, with the same "may be slow" note it gives other slow lines. Large counts are refused now, and so is a count on a look-ahead or right after an open-ended repeat. Short ones like `\d{4}` still work. The lines of one list also share a single budget, so a hundred heavy lines can't add up to a slow chat. A line like that from an older list or a settings file stays in the editor and in backups, but the chat skips it without running it. A repeat that can only stop in one place, like the spaces in `/airdrop\s+0x[a-f0-9]{40}/`, isn't counted as many ways into the count after it, so filters for wallet addresses work. That shortcut isn't taken for a letter written by its number, like `\x61`, or one that matches two letters when case is ignored, like ß or ẞ, so `/\x61+a{1000}!/` is turned away like `/a+a{1000}!/`. Checking that shortcut reads each pair of characters once and keeps the answer, so a list of a hundred wallet lines is ready in a moment instead of holding up the first message after it's saved.
* **Telegram:** A switch you flip while a settings import is running stays the way you left it. Before, the switch and the setting Telegram was running could snap back while your change was still saved, so the next start disagreed with what you saw. Only the switches the file names wait for the import now, and every settings page that's open shows how it ended.
* **Telegram:** A settings import that changes **Use system font**, **AMOLED black**, **Disable pull to archive**, **Hide Contacts tab** or the **Emoji next to the chat list title** now brings up the Restart Telegram row, just like flipping one of them by hand. A file that sets a switch back to what Telegram is running clears that one, and an import that fails doesn't add any.
* **Telegram:** Saving a filter list, the translation service, the sticker size or the emoji next to the chat list title no longer freezes the settings screen while the phone writes it. The dialog dims its buttons until the save is done, so a second tap doesn't start another, and it only closes once the save worked. If it didn't, what you typed stays and the list goes back to the size that's saved. Chats keep using the old value until the new one is actually saved. A save you make while a settings import is still running waits with a short note and keeps what you typed.
* **Telegram:** **Clear diagnostic data** and its undo do their file work in the background now, so slow storage doesn't hold the settings screen. The row waits while it works and ignores extra taps. If putting the data back fails, the row still offers to try again. Whatever HushTelegram records in the meantime doesn't wait for the files either.
* **Telegram:** Patching is faster. Most patches used to read every instruction in Telegram on their own to find the few methods they change. Now the app is read once per patching session, and each patch only looks inside the classes that mention what it's searching for. On a PC, the default patches for Telegram 13.0.2 took about 32 seconds instead of 52, and the patches themselves went from about 34 seconds to 15. In Morphe Manager on a two-core Android 14 emulator, 67 patches on the same Telegram took about 51 seconds instead of 111 to 116. What each patch changes stays the same, and so does every check that makes it refuse a build it doesn't recognize.
* **Telegram:** Searching HushTelegram settings for "null" no longer turns up rows that just don't have a line under their title.
* **Telegram:** **Notification status on this phone** now gives Telegram's reply to each account's push sign-up on its own line, with Firebase and UnifiedPush apart and how long ago the reply came. Before, it kept only the newest reply, so one account's refusal could hide behind another account's success. Accounts show as 1, 2 and so on, never by name or number, and a reply that can't be tied to one account isn't shown as anyone's. The diagnostic report carries the same lines.
* **Telegram:** **Play voice messages one at a time** has a second switch on the Playback page, **Keep voice messages quiet while locked**. With it on, voice and round video messages don't start, resume or skip to the next one while your phone is locked, whether the tap comes from headphones, a car, the notification or the lock screen, and a short note says to unlock first. One that's already playing finishes. Music and other videos play as usual. It starts off.
* **Telegram:** **Faster downloads** has a second switch on the Playback page, **Hold automatic downloads on Data Saver**. With it on, while Android's Data Saver is on and the network is metered, Telegram doesn't start photos, videos, files, voice messages, music or stories downloading on its own, and the next song and upcoming stories aren't loaded ahead. Automatic downloads in Telegram's download queue stop when the hold starts and pick up again once it lifts, though one a chat had already started as it showed the message gets to finish. What you tap still downloads. A video you open streams without being saved for later, so it doesn't land in Telegram's Downloads, and a download from Telegram's in-app browser asks first. Both work that way when automatic downloads are off, too. With Data Saver off, Telegram allowed to use data freely, an unmetered network or no network, Telegram's own rules apply. The hold notices the switch, Data Saver or the network changing right away, and the row shows what Android reports when you open the page. It starts off, and it doesn't hold anything while HushTelegram is paused.
* **Telegram:** Settings say which account they work on. **Folders by chat type** works on the account you have open. A chat or message you turn on for outside translation stays on only in the account you turned it on in. **Keep drafts on this phone** covers every account. **Export settings** lists what a settings file leaves out in your build, the translation service and its key, the settings lock and a hidden Quick setups row among them, and says your chats, drafts and kept messages aren't in it.
* **Telegram:** The **Hide messages by keyword** list editors have a **Try** button. Type or paste a message under the list and it tells you which line would hide it, numbered the way you see the lines, or that none would. It reads the list the way a chat does, unsaved changes included, so the first line that matches is the one named. A line that can't be used gets the same note Save gives. The message you try isn't saved, logged or sent, and it's gone when the editor closes. Autofill doesn't see it either. **Try** waits for its answer before it takes another tap, and when the phone is too busy to check, it asks you to try again in a moment rather than freezing the screen. A check that fails says the same instead of showing nothing.
* **Telegram:** The settings home page has a **Changed switches** row just above More settings. It counts the switches that aren't the way they started and opens a page with only those, each under the name of its page, including ones that start on and were turned off. Flip one there and it's back the way it started and off the list. The settings lock and a change that needs a restart work there just like on the switch's own page.
* **Telegram:** After a **Quick setups** choice changes switches, its note says you can undo it, and Quick setups shows an **Undo the last setup** card. The card names what the choice turned on and off, and how many switches were already set or couldn't change. Undo puts back only the switches you haven't touched since, through the same steps as a tap, so the lock and restart notes still apply. It only moves switches, so the chats' translate choices a switch cleared stay cleared. A settings import ends the undo. If an undo couldn't put everything back, the card lists only what's left.
* **Telegram:** **Notification status on this phone** splits its details into three parts, each with its own fix. The first is what Android allows, now including whether it restricts Telegram in the background and whether battery optimization is on. The second is the push service, with the UnifiedPush app's state when your build has it. The third is what Telegram answered each account, and an APP_PUSH_APIKEY_MISSING refusal now explains that it's set up on Telegram's side, not on your phone. When Android holds Telegram back, a button takes you to where that's changed. That's App info, or before Android 12, Android's battery optimization list when battery optimization is all that applies, since App info only reaches it a few taps in there. Nothing gets changed for you, and anything that can't be read says Unknown.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** Every build graph this repository owns uses Guava 33.7.2 now, the release that fixes CVE-2026-102554. That includes the lint and annotation tools the Android plugin loads on its own. The patcher's classpath still says 33.5.0, because that's what Morphe Manager and the CLI run with, and the dependency report keeps it that way.
* **Tooling:** The selection check lets a selection with `Black and white launch logo` rewrite exactly the two values it changes in Telegram's dark launch theme, the splash background to black and the splash icon to the logo it adds, and checks the icon names that logo. Every other selection still has to leave Telegram's values as they were.
* **Tooling:** The selection check expects the UnifiedPush receiver's fifth action, `TEMP_UNAVAILABLE`, which the patch has declared since it started following the connector contract. Every selection with UnifiedPush in it was failing that check, the default one included.
* **Tooling:** The build runs on Gradle 9.8.1 now. 9.7.1 was inside three of Gradle's own high severity advisories, and 9.8.1 is the release that fixes them.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push hook now stops a push whose ref lines aren't what git sends, instead of reading them as nothing to check.
* **Tooling:** The advisory gates stop when OSV sends back something that isn't a real answer. An error object used to read as "no advisories", and the gate passed without checking anything.
* **Tooling:** The build advisory scan now holds the Gradle version to Gradle's own published advisories, so a wrapper inside a known high severity range is refused. OSV doesn't cover the build tool, which is why a clean library scan said nothing about it.
* **Tooling:** Two device builds can run at once without stepping on each other. Each works in its own folder, so a second run can't overwrite or delete the first one's files.
* **Tooling:** A device install only goes ahead under a lease in the machine's shared lease folder. A lease kept somewhere else doesn't count anymore.
* **Tooling:** A device build now waits its turn in the machine's build queue before it starts patching, and the patcher runs with a capped heap and two processors so it doesn't crowd out builds already running.
* **Tooling:** A release can't skip the build advisory scan anymore. Release preflight and the build stage both generate the dependency report under strict checksum verification, run the scan, and stop on a build tool or library it refuses. The release gate also reads the Gradle version recorded in an SBOM and holds it to the same advisory list, even when the OSV check is skipped.
* **Tooling:** Patching now checks each extension stub it writes the way Android's verifier will, and stops with the stub's name if one would be turned down. The side menu's name stub was: one register held your user on one path and your name on the other, so Android refused the whole side menu and Telegram closed on the first swipe.
* **Tooling:** Morphe Manager now lists what changed in the release your Telegram was patched with, the way it does for older ones. The release's index stage puts every bullet but the Tooling ones under What's new in the bundle description, and the release facts check reads only the text above that list.
* **Tooling:** A release no longer stops when the GitHub description names no version, patch count or Telegram build. That description is left as written, and one that names any of them is still kept current.
* **Tooling:** A device build now clears out what a killed one left behind. When `patch-for-device.ps1` starts, it deletes any `run-` folder in the output folder that no running build owns, the argument file with the signing password included. Each build records its process and start time in its folder, so a build that's still running is never touched. One whose process can't be read, such as a build started as administrator, is left alone too.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.0.3 from telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android). The [official beta](https://telegram.org/dl/android/apk-public-beta) 13.0.3 works too, and both have version code 71839. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from v0.0.17? That one was built for 13.0.2, so patch the new 13.0.3 APK and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put one over the other. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram won't send you a login code, register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps). Use only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

1360 runtime tests and 487 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints. All 68 patches applied without forcing to Telegram 13.0.3 and to the 13.0.3 beta, both version code 71839. The release receipt checked each patched app's manifest, native libraries, resources and alignment.

On a Samsung phone running Android 16, a 13.0.3 build from the same patch code installed over the 13.0.2 one and stayed signed in. A swipe on the chat list's title bar opened the side menu, its HushTelegram settings and Settings rows opened their pages, and Back closed it. The patched 13.0.3 beta started and opened HushTelegram settings on an Android emulator.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.14
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.14 has 19 patches for Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

This one moves to Threads 451 and gives HushThreads settings a new look. All 11 pages are redesigned, and a long press on the Threads logo at the top of your feed opens them. Flip a switch that needs a restart and a Restart row shows up, so you don't have to close Threads by hand.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#8](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/8) hit "Sorry, we weren't able to load that website" when tapping a Threads post in the regular Instagram app. That message is Instagram's own. It only hands posts over to a Threads signed by Meta, and a patched Threads carries your Morphe Manager key. The README's Help section explains it now, and opening the post from inside Threads still works.

## Threads

- This release patches Threads 451.0.0.51.80 only, the newest stable version. 450.0.0.51.78 isn't offered any more, so update Threads to 451 before you patch. Sharing, saved media, autoplay and dark backgrounds follow the new build's layout.
- Search, buttons and choices show a visible focus outline. Switches and actions use the same corner scale as the settings cards.
- Download and report choosers close when their page is removed. Diagnostic exports describe the right folder on Android 9, and clearing logs offers Restore diagnostic data while recovery is available.
- Both backup actions explain why they're unavailable during an import or export.
- Link status checks the post domains declared by Threads. Unrelated chat and login domains no longer make working post links appear disabled. Reports still list every declared domain.
- The logo's long press has an action label in the app's language for screen readers.
- Flip a switch that needs a restart and a Restart row shows up at the top of settings. Tap it and Threads reopens on the page you were on. Importing a settings file that changes one of those switches brings up the same row.
- The Support HushThreads row at the bottom of settings is just its name now, without the line of text under it.
- Redesigned all 11 settings pages with separate cards and blue icons. Search and Pause stay at the top of the home page, and long descriptions wrap without hiding controls. About and diagnostic exports retain the full build details.
- No time limit is dimmed until Keep feed position on return is on. Its saved choice stays intact when that switch is off.
- Downloads has a Saves section that says when nothing is in progress. Active saves still show progress and Cancel.
- Long-press the Threads logo at the top of your home feed to open HushThreads settings right over the feed. It works while HushThreads is paused, and a plain tap on the logo does what it always did.

## Docs

- The README's Help section now explains why the regular Instagram app says "Sorry, we weren't able to load that website" for a post when your Threads is patched.
- The README is much shorter now and keeps to what you need to install and use HushThreads. The long version, with every build and test note, is still in the repository history.

## Tooling

- Source updates can keep an Unreleased changelog while Manager serves the previous release. The published release's date and history remain required.
- The signed-app check now requires the logo's settings action exactly once and rejects missing, duplicated or misdirected calls.
- Updated the signed-app check for the redesigned settings. About and reports still have to carry the exact bundle identity.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.14 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Patch the arm64-v8a bundle of Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (version code 512108444). 450 isn't offered any more, so download 451 and patch that one. v0.0.13 is the last release that patches 450.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

859 runtime tests and 258 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 19 patches applied without forcing to Threads 451.0.0.51.80, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.
